decisions.reason: As a flagship close to the core offer and still highlighted on the home page, it is tied to visible prior commitment and the firm's stated direction, so withdrawal is very unlikely.

The oncology risk management software extends the firm's integrated QA and software capabilities, and management can justify giving it more time by pointing to adoption and workflow cycles in hospitals.
This CT phantom fits the established imaging QA business and, as a very recent launch in an expanding firm, is likely to be retained while results are still interpreted as early-stage.
Because it is more distant from the historical core its fit is weaker, but the firm has already invested in launching and publicly listing it, which makes management inclined to continue for now.
This mammography phantom is also peripheral and therefore more vulnerable than core products, yet the recency of launch and desire to justify the market entry still favor keeping it another year.

As a flagship multi-model line that supports the firm's announced move toward broader measurement and integrated imaging QA, it carries strong strategic and reputational commitment and is unlikely to be dropped.
